podcast.title: 21st Century Descendant of Tweetpop
podcast.body: Bedroom Pop is recognized as a 21st-century evolution directly stemming from Tweetpop, made possible by the widespread availability of affordable and powerful laptops, coupled with free or inexpensive recording software, microphones, and other necessary gear. This technological accessibility allows artists to create high-quality music in intimate bedroom settings, reflecting deeply personal thoughts and exhibiting characteristics that are dreamy, introspective, sensitive, and vulnerable, mirroring Tweetpop's core appeal. "This is a 21st century descendant from Tweet that was made possible by the availability of cheap and powerful laptops, along with free, or at least inexpensive, recording software, microphones, and other associated gear."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: DIY Home Recording Ethos
podcast.body: Bedroom Pop emerged as a genre fueled by the increased accessibility of home recording software and equipment like GarageBand, enabling artists to create professional-sounding music in their own homes and distribute it online for free. "The rise in the availability of home recording software and equipment made it possible for almost anyone to create professional sounding recordings in their bedroom, hence the name."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.title: Emergence with Home Recording Gear
podcast.body: Bedroom Pop emerged as a distinct genre, greatly facilitated by the widespread availability of cheap and powerful home recording equipment. This accessibility allowed artists to record music independently, often within their homes, cultivating a sound that inherently embraced its homemade origins, imperfections, and raw authenticity. "More low-fi, something called Bedroom Pop, a resurgence in sounds like shoegays, new flavors of hip hop."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 100 Greatest Rock Moments of the Millennium So Far - Part 5: (60-51)

podcast.title: Historical Antecedents
podcast.body: While prominent in the 2010s, Bedroom Pop has roots dating back to the late 1960s with acts like The Beach Boys, and also connects to 1980s Dreampop and 1990s lo-fi slacker sounds and attitudes. "Heck an argument can be made that the Beach Boys were making this kind of music in the late 1960s. And there's a definite connection to both Dreampop, which was a product of the 80s, and the low-fi slacker sounds in attitude of the 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.title: LGBTQ+ Community Connection
podcast.body: The intimate and personal nature of Bedroom Pop makes it a significant medium for artists, particularly within the LGBTQ+ community, to explore personal themes and experiences. "Another thing we should say about bedroom pop is it ties to the LGBTQ plus community. Because the style is so intimate and so personal, some artists use it to explore these particular themes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.title: Lo-Fi Spin-Off with Modern Tools (Present)
podcast.body: Bedroom Pop is recognized as a modern spin-off of low-fidelity music, characterized by home recordings primarily made using a laptop rather than older Portastudio cassette units. This genre is often described as dreamy, intimate, and introspective, reflecting a continuation of the lo-fi spirit with contemporary digital tools. While not all bedroom pop is inherently lo-fi, it maintains a close connection to the home recording ethos. "This is music consisting of home recordings using a laptop instead of an old school port studio cassette unit. It can be dreamy, intimate, and introspective. But not all bedroom pop is low five. You'll know it when you hear it."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Synthetic and Vulnerable Sound
podcast.body: Generally, Bedroom Pop features synthetic sounds from electronic keyboards, drums, and loops, occasionally with acoustic guitar, and vocals/lyrics often convey vulnerability, insecurity, and naiveness. "Generally, the sounds are synthetic, electronic keyboards, drums, loops, maybe an acoustic guitar here and there. You may also pick up elements of vulnerability, insecurity, and naiveness with the vocals and the lyrics."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres

podcast.title: Unfiltered and Intimate Production
podcast.body: A defining characteristic of Bedroom Pop is its unfiltered nature, lacking intermediaries like producers or record labels, which allows for extreme do-it-yourself music making with an emphasis on intimacy, raw emotion, and sparse production. "One of the attractive things about making music in this style is that it can be completely unfiltered. There are no intermediaries like a producer or a record label that might want to offer suggestions or edits or notes."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of the 2010s Part 3: The New Genres
